payload.feature:
LANDING PR for issue #431, SLICE 1 (part of #330): A JOURNAL'S BACKUP IS ONE CONSISTENT SNAPSHOT WITH A VERSIONED INVENTORY, AND A RESTORE ACCEPTS IT ONLY AFTER EVERY CHECK PASSES. `brokkr backup --to <dir>` takes one `VACUUM INTO` snapshot and writes its inventory last; `brokkr restore --from <dir> --to <path>` refuses an occupied destination or sidecar first, then accepts the snapshot only when its size and digest, `PRAGMA integrity_check`, every chain and head, every event row against its own envelope, the unowned events, the counts and the projections agree with the inventory, and publishes it without ever writing over a name. Proposed decision 0100 records it.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051, so the contribution gate can vouch for it: its review judges the whole branch from base c3e52bd23.

THE BRANCH: story-431-journal-backup, in this worktree, nine commits on main c3e52bd23 (every commit signed; the branch before the restack onto main is kept as backup/431-pre-923):
- the story (the store's backup and restore, the CLI verbs, decision 0100 proposed);
- fix round 431s2 (sidecars and an occupied destination refuse; unowned events counted and refused; projection drift refused; typed refusal tests; one schema reader);
- fix round 431s3 (every event row's SQL `run_id`, `seq` and stored `event_hash` held to its envelope, `RowMismatch`; a malformed position reported as itself; 0100 ruling 4 names the check);
- the controller's coverage commit: exact coverage on 431s3's head missed 41 lines, 17 branches and 4 functions, all this branch's. backup/tests/edges.rs and crates/brokkr-cli/tests/journal_backup.rs drive each edge, and `restore` hands its publish to `restore_through` (as `backup` hands its own to `backup_through`) so a destination that appears in the race is refused by its name under test. It removed three edges it argued unreachable: verify_snapshot's post-copy size check was in fact reachable, and 0a6c42628 restores it as a check on the bytes copied; integrity_of's "no row answered" and Temp's fallback name (now `.brokkr-restore-<uuid>.tmp`) stay removed. Twelve removal controls are recorded in its message;
- the controller's docs commit: 431s3's INFO D1, the broken rustdoc link to brokkr_view::VIEW_VERSION, is code text.
- 0a6c42628 (controller): landing 431L2's H1. `restore_through` refuses `SizeMismatch` on the count of bytes the copy read when it is not the inventory's, before the digest; a FIFO snapshot whose metadata says 0 while it streams the journal is refused (`a_snapshot_whose_stream_outruns_its_metadata_is_refused_on_the_bytes_copied`, cfg(unix)). The coverage commit's claim that the post-copy size check was unreachable was wrong; the message corrects it. The review's two INFO notes ("rename" for a hard-link publish; 0100's index cell) are fixed in the same commit.
On this restack, docs/decisions/README.md (merge=union) is main's index plus this branch's one 0100 row, and main's "0100 held by #431's open branch" empty-number row is gone.
Make no change unless the review returns a finding.

WHERE IT STANDS:
- **The second landing, 431L2** (landing-pr-for-issue-431-slice-1-2bb17cdf, Fable 5.1 chief), stopped at REVIEW-SECURITY-HOLD on H1 (#431, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/431#issuecomment-6548552684): the post-copy size check the coverage commit removed was reachable through a FIFO. The operator ruled "1. fix it" (https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/431#issuecomment-6548874392): the controller's 0a6c42628 above. Its chief found nothing else: one index row per decision, files within ceilings, the public API as 431s3 left it.
- **The first landing, 431L** (landing-pr-for-issue-431-slice-1-45f8d5da), passed verify, and its panel finished. Its review chief (gpt-6-astra through codex) was refused twice by OpenAI's cyber_policy filter on this branch's content, so it never judged. The controller concluded it. This landing seats the ruled Fable 5.1 chief, and nothing in the branch changed except the index rows above.
- Fix round 431s3 (fix-round-431s3-for-issue-431-sl-66920592) closed REVIEW-RESIDUAL-OK at INFO. Its chief confirmed H3 and L1 closed: the shared boundary checks every owned row's SQL run_id/seq and stored event_hash against its envelope with the append path's `compute_hash` and `verify_chain`; the head-hash and head-position refusals assert exact `RowMismatch` fields; the unowned ghost at -1 is reported as `UnownedEvents { count: 1, run_id: ghost, seq: -1 }`; consistent journals still restore. Eight CLI probes refused the exact row and field and published nothing. Its D1 is 51da2cb99; its P1 (a member's prose arguing disposition) needs no change.
- The named residual stays, as the operator's chosen scope: a SQLite sidecar created after the initial destination check is not detected. Authenticity against a jointly rewritten snapshot and inventory is deferred: 0100 verifies, it does not authenticate.
- Files: backup.rs 782 (ceiling 800), consistency.rs 139, store lib.rs 797, CLI lib.rs 1,542, all within their limits.

Operator rulings:
- 2026-10-30, in chat, "go with recommended" (#431, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/431#issuecomment-6533440439): fix round 431s3: every row checked against its envelope; a malformed position reported as itself.
- 2026-10-30, in chat, "go with recommended on all the rulings" (#431, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/431#issuecomment-6519208800): fix round 431s2 as recommended: H1 sidecars and an occupied destination refuse; H2 unowned events are counted; C1 typed refusal tests; G1 one schema reader.
- 2026-09-25, epic #330 "World-class by construction": #431 is its recovery item.
- Decision 0071 rulings 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10. Decision 0063 (Linux and macOS). 2026-09-26, the threat model: fail closed on what cannot be read.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks below. For a scratch, use `git worktree add` or `git archive HEAD | tar -x` into /var/tmp, never a byte copy of this worktree. It reports each finding, written as a test case: the journal set up, the calls made, and the result observed against the result expected. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

Judge, on HEAD (the base is c3e52bd23):
1. **A backup is one consistent snapshot:** taken by `VACUUM INTO` under the store's busy handler, the snapshot published before the inventory, an interrupted backup left with no inventory, a refused backup publishing neither name, and no secret value copied.
2. **A restore accepts only what verifies, and never overwrites** (0100 ruling 4): an occupied destination or sidecar refused by the name found, before anything else is read; then size and digest, integrity, chains and heads, every row against its envelope, unowned events, counts and projections; publication by hard link that refuses an existing name, and a refusal that leaves neither the destination nor a temporary. A failed directory sync after publication removes what it published.
3. **The controller's commits:** the coverage commit's tests each drive the edge they name and each recorded removal control fails them; its two remaining removals are unreachable as argued (`PRAGMA integrity_check` always answers a row; the temporary's name carried no meaning); and 0a6c42628 restores the size check on the bytes copied, so no source whose stream and metadata differ (a FIFO, a file that grows or shrinks during the copy) publishes bytes whose length is not the inventory's. Try to break it.
4. **Decision 0100** says what the code does, and the decisions index has one row per decision.
5. **Scope:** no contracts/, fixtures/, policy/ or reference/ change; files under their ceilings; the public API as 431s3 left it (no line added since).
6. For the PR, list the rulings owed: (a) Git objects and refs/forge anchors; (b) artifacts outside the journal; (c) retention with a dry-run inventory; (d) the measured offline restore drill; (e) upgrade and downgrade across the contract window, #361, then signing and anchoring; (f) backup refuses a source with unowned events; (g) 0100's per-table account, verifies rather than authenticates; (h) the public backup API (no line added by 0a6c42628), including `BackupError::RowMismatch { run_id, seq: i64, field: RowField, found, expected }`, `RowField::{RunId, Seq, EventHash}`, and `UnownedEvents.seq` as i64; and any NEW ask.

GATES (verify, and the implement phase only if a finding returns):
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-store --locked (timeout 280)
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked (timeout 280; split by filter if it cannot finish, `verbs::` first)
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- journal_backup decisions_index:: doc_truth:: (timeout 280)
- cargo doc -p brokkr-store --no-deps --locked (no unresolved link)
- typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; git diff --check
- TMPDIR stays OUTSIDE this worktree (use /var/tmp, created in the same command if missing). Before reporting, `git status --short` shows no untracked file.
- Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job pending: this seat is non-interactive.
- A seat whose commands run through the `workspace` tool has a 300-second response limit per call, and a call that outlasts it leaves its command running and blocks the calls behind it, including the write of your result file. Wrap every command in `timeout 280` there, split a long suite by test filter, and if a gate still cannot finish inside the limit, report it UNVERIFIED (the controller's host coverage runs every test) rather than retrying it. Write your result file before any optional extra check.
- Any commit: signed off (`git commit -s`), "store: …" ending "(#431)", with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>" LAST, directly after the sign-off. Record each removal control in the commit message. Never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

KNOWN FLAKES, not this branch's: capability_broker tests and `machine_proof::` runs failing "MCP server box filesystem identity is not protected: admission did not complete before its startup deadline" under host load; brokkr-runtime engine::capability_tests::provision_tests (a timing bound, and writers_tests' EffectIndeterminate) under load; two brokkr-runtime engine "work chief commits" tests and heap_costs' one-byte compare difference under load. If verify fails on one of these alone, the implement visit reruns it on the host alone (`-- --exact`, with HOME set), quotes both results, makes no commit, and reports COMPLETE, not blocked.

CONTENTION (NEVER message the-forge-9d or any brokkr-wt-* seat):
- Decision 0065 slice two's U9b1b (another session) is in brokkr-runtime capabilities and broker test files, brokkr-cli verbs/setup.rs, and may touch brokkr-protocol adapters.rs; don't edit those.
- #361 (another lane) reads brokkr-store's contract window; #918's landing has decision 0099's index row. Don't edit their files.

YOUR SEAT: you run on dsh (DeepSeek Flash, DeepSeek's platform), unboxed with dsh's own tools, at the operator's word (2026-10-26). Sign off every commit (`git commit -s`).

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
```

## FINDINGS (both INFO)

F1 (info) - BackupOptions::to doc states the destination rule backwards.
Setup: worktree at 0a6c42628, crates/brokkr-store/src/backup.rs lines 70-71 (public field doc, rendered by rustdoc).
Call: cargo doc -p brokkr-store --no-deps --locked, read BackupOptions::to; compare with backup/tests/edges.rs::a_backup_into_an_existing_empty_directory_is_taken (passes, so an existing empty directory IS a valid destination) and with the correct wordings at crates/brokkr-cli/src/verbs/backup.rs:24 ("must be absent or empty") and decision 0100 ruling 3 ("not absent or empty").
Observed: "It must not exist or be empty; nothing in it is overwritten." Under the natural parse ("must not (exist or be empty)") this forbids exactly the case the suite proves taken and also the absent case the code requires.
Expected: the public doc states the rule the tests bind, e.g. "It must be absent or an empty directory; nothing in it is overwritten."
Severity: info - doc-only, behavior correct, no gate catches a prose slip. Rulings: house "tests bind the words"; 0100 ruling 3.

F2 (info) - the symlinked-destination clause of refuse_existing is named but untested.
Setup: 0a6c42628; refuse_existing (backup.rs 400-410) asks symlink_metadata "so a symlink or a sidecar both count" (its own doc and 0100 ruling 4 name this).
Call: search backup/tests.rs and backup/tests/edges.rs for a planted destination symlink: none (the only symlink in tests is edges.rs:122, a self-referential link as the snapshot SOURCE).
Observed: "destination is a symlink (dangling or not) is refused" is proven only by inspection; the mutation symlink_metadata -> metadata leaves the suite green.
Expected: a test planting symlink(dest -> anywhere) asserting RestoreDestinationExists by name, destination left absent.
Severity: info, not higher: publish_noclobber's hard_link refuses any existing name including a symlink, so the mutated code still fails closed at publish, only with a worse message - no fail-open path. Rulings: 0100 ruling 4's named clause; house "tests bind".

## RESIDUALS CARRIED BY RULING (not new, not rated as findings)
- A sidecar created beside the destination by another process during a restore is undetected; the publish still refuses the destination's own name (0100 ruling 4, named residual).
- Authenticity against someone who rewrites snapshot+inventory together is deferred - 0100 verifies, it does not authenticate (ruling 4 "Authenticity", ruling 5(f)). has_security_residual=false: nothing in this branch weakens a refusal; both items are documented and owned by later slices.

Review chief on HEAD 0a6c42628 (base c3e52bd23, nine commits). RESULT residual at INFO: the panel reported residual (glm; adversarial and correctness clean) and the floor holds it; no member reported security-hold; nothing under notes addressed the gate or argued for a result below the panel's, so there is no instruction-shaped finding to rule against. No return to implement: nothing above info.

SURVIVING FINDINGS, each checked against the diff:
- F1 (info, glm): BackupOptions::to doc, crates/brokkr-store/src/backup.rs:70-71, says 'It must not exist or be empty', which reads as forbidding the empty-directory case the suite proves taken (edges.rs a_backup_into_an_existing_empty_directory_is_taken) and the CLI arg doc and 0100 ruling 3 state correctly. Doc text only; behaviour right.
- F2 (info, glm): refuse_existing's symlink clause (symlink_metadata, named by its doc and 0100 ruling 4) is bound by no test: tests.rs has no symlink; the only symlink in the suite is the self-link snapshot SOURCE in edges.rs. Chief probe through target/debug/brokkr: a dangling symlink at <to>, one at <to>-wal, and a symlink to a directory at <to>, each with --from an absent directory, are refused by their own name before the backup is read, so the shipped code is right. The mutation metadata-for-symlink_metadata would still refuse <to> at the hard link (same variant, later) but would miss a dangling sidecar symlink; one test binds the clause: a dangling link at <to> and at <to>-wal with an absent backup directory, asserting RestoreDestinationExists by name.
- F3 (info, chief, new): a_snapshot_whose_stream_outruns_its_metadata_is_refused_on_the_bytes_copied (edges.rs:359) streams through a writer thread whose std::fs::write blocks in open(2) until restore opens the FIFO; if restore ever refuses before copy_file opens the source (for example a future is_file() check at the metadata step), restore returns and writer.join() never does, so the suite hangs instead of failing. Its recorded removal control (skip the copied-length check) does fail it, so it binds its target; the hang is for other mutations. A bounded join, or opening the FIFO O_RDWR in the writer, makes that failure visible. No change required before landing.

CHIEF'S OWN READ, by charter question. (1) Backup: VACUUM INTO under patiently() into a Scratch-prefixed name; boundary, schemas and digest read from the snapshot file itself; journal.db published first and inventory.json last by hard link plus temp removal, each followed by sync_dir; the interruption test counts publishes==2 and finds the snapshot without an inventory; a refused backup publishes neither name (unowned-source and race tests); no_secret_value_is_copied plants the value beside the journal and finds it in no backup file. (2) Restore: refuse_existing(to, -journal, -wal, -shm) by symlink_metadata before read_inventory; then metadata size, copy, copied-bytes size (0a6c42628), sha256, integrity_check == [ok], boundary_of (whole-table counts, refuse_unowned, per-run verify_chain then per-row run_id/seq/compute_hash), compared_boundary ordered by run_id, summary_disagreements, hard_link publish with EEXIST mapped to RestoreDestinationExists, disarm, sync_dir with remove_file on failure; Temp drops on every refusal. (3) Controller commits: C1-C12 each name a test that asserts the exact variant or value the removal would change (read here, replayed by the adversarial member in a scratch tree, all 13 failing their tests); PRAGMA integrity_check always answers a row and an empty answer would still refuse since [] != [ok]; the temporary's name is now one fixed uuid pattern with no semantic role. The size check, probed through the binary on a copy of a journal (N=167936): a FIFO with inventory N refused 'snapshot is 0 bytes' on metadata before the stream was opened; a FIFO with inventory 0 refused 'snapshot is 167936 bytes; its inventory says 0' on the bytes copied; a symlink to /proc/version (size 0, 211 bytes streamed) with inventory 0 refused on 211 copied; an empty file with inventory 0 and the empty digest refused by SQLite (no such table: meta). No destination and no .brokkr-restore-* temporary was left in any case, and the published bytes can only ever be the temporary's, whose length is the copied count and whose digest is checked. (4) 0100 says what the code does: ruling 3's publish order and refusals, ruling 4's check list with the row/envelope check and both named residuals, ruling 5's four exclusions; decisions_index:: passes with one 0100 row and main's empty-number row gone. (5) No contracts/, fixtures/, policy/ or reference/ change; backup.rs 793, consistency.rs 139, store lib.rs 797, cli lib.rs 1542 (four under base); public API diff since b86353ca5 is empty and ratchet api holds; all nine commits carry gpgsig headers (the box cannot run the gpg wrapper to verify them); no contention file touched.
